note: SEED ONLY. Real org names/categories/eligibility/hours are modeled for the Oct 1 sim; many are needs_verification and NONE carry public contact info (phone/website/address) yet. Enrich + verify before public use. _internal.* fields are staff-only — do not publish.

orgs.public_description: The local clinic where a long-standing provider relationship lives — and where many journeys begin with the words "you'll need a referral." A sliding-scale community health center serving the county.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Blue Ridge Health provider and front-desk staff — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: A trusted pediatric provider — often the first formal door a worried parent knocks on, and the start of many behavioral health waits.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Blue Ridge Health pediatric provider — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: A counselor or teacher a family already trusts. Often the first place a worry is said out loud — and a bridge to formal care when the bridge holds.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a school counselor — could be paired with a Blue Ridge Health school-based health rep if confirmed

orgs.public_description: The room where the county actually gathers — potlucks, meetings, quiet conversations by the coffee urn where needs first get spoken.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a community center coordinator

orgs.public_description: A congregation that has carried casseroles, rides, and quiet checks-ins for generations. Trust lives here before any need is named.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a pastor or congregation member

orgs.public_description: The monthly, client-choice food pathway — a week's groceries you pick yourself — and the broader safety-net door when food is only part of the crisis: rent and utility assistance, clothing, and basic needs under one roof. Reliable, but it runs on a schedule and a process.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Sharing House coordinator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: A same-day, short-notice food access point — fewer forms, faster shelf. Used when the standard pantry pathway is too slow for tonight's table. Serves hot meals no-questions-asked and reaches remote areas of the county.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Bread of Life volunteer — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: The community van, volunteer drivers, and ride coordination — the difference between an appointment made and an appointment reached. A fixed route and dedicated medical transportation, alongside senior transportation services.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Transylvania County Transportation ride coordinator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: Where referrals get processed, faxed, re-faxed, and tracked — essential and invisible until it stalls. Not a staffed table but a bottleneck the family passes through; the delay is the point. The active navigation service lives at the Community Health Worker door.
orgs.represented_by_note: (Unmanned friction point — no org table; the real navigation service is the Community Health Worker door)

orgs.public_description: The out-of-county cardiology practice. Good care, real distance — an hour round trip on a good day, plus whatever the paperwork requires.
orgs.physical_location_event: Far corner — table 7 (deliberately the farthest walk)
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing specialist office staff

orgs.public_description: The county's behavioral health capacity: skilled, caring, and carrying a waitlist measured in months. Youth substance-misuse prevention has its own dedicated, grant-funded support — separate from adult treatment or detox, which the county does not currently have.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a behavioral health intake coordinator — CARE Coalition rep could join for the youth-prevention angle specifically

orgs.public_description: County public health: immunizations, WIC, home visits, and quiet system-holding that most residents never see.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Transylvania Public Health nurse — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: Patient portals, PDF forms, upload buttons, and password resets — the invisible tollbooth between a referral and an appointment.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing "the portal" (a laptop and a stack of forms)

orgs.public_description: One door among many in the local network — not a clinic, not a charity counter, a place where your story gets heard once and carried forward.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Resilience Hub navigator

orgs.public_description: A person, not a place: someone who knows both the family and the system, and makes calls that turn cold intakes into expected arrivals.
orgs.physical_location_event: Roving — look for the goldenrod sash
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a community health worker / connector

orgs.public_description: Where the hours come from — and where every daytime appointment collides with a shift schedule that doesn't bend.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a shift supervisor

orgs.public_description: The kitchen table between appointments. Nothing happens here — which is exactly the problem. Waiting is where momentum, and sometimes health, quietly erodes.
orgs.represented_by_note: Unstaffed — a table, two chairs, a phone that does not ring

orgs.public_description: The door that is always open — which is why the whole system's gaps eventually arrive here, at the highest cost and the hardest hour.
orgs.physical_location_event: Far side room — bright lights on
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing ED triage staff — do not brand as a specific real hospital without direct confirmation

orgs.public_description: Food that comes to you, on a rotating schedule, because getting to a fixed pantry is itself the barrier. A rotating pantry at a different location each Thursday, with partners providing fresh produce.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Hunger Coalition distribution volunteer — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Home Repair & Recovery (Transylvania Habitat for Humanity)
orgs.public_description: Tropical Storm Helene (Sept. 2024) recovery repair support — the door between "the tarp holds" and an actual timeline for fixing it. Volunteer labor and materials mean the queue moves in weeks and months, not days.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Habitat for Humanity recovery-repair coordinator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: The county's Spanish-language connector, and for many families the only door where the phone is always answered in Spanish. A translator, a vouching voice, and a warm handoff into a system not built with them in mind.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing an El Centro staff member — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: The county's actual front door for Medicaid, food assistance, and emergency energy help — the paperwork that decides what a family can afford before any other door matters.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a DSS eligibility caseworker — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Housing Crisis Support (The Haven of Transylvania County)
orgs.public_description: The door for a family with nowhere to sleep tonight — shelter first, a path back to permanent housing second. An overnight shelter offering intake, meals, laundry, and referral toward permanent or transitional housing.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Haven intake coordinator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Adult Behavioral Health (Meridian Behavioral Health Services)
orgs.public_description: Outpatient counseling and substance-use support for adults — real, local, and separate from the county's youth-focused behavioral health capacity. Not a detox or residential program — the county does not currently have one.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Meridian outpatient counselor — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: The door that fixes the portal problem instead of just naming it — a refurbished device, a broadband subsidy, someone to sit with you through the login.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Through the Trees technician — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: Training, credentials, and a path to a job that pays enough to make the rest of this easier — not a hiring hall, a bridge into one.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Chamber workforce-development liaison — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.public_description: The county's coordinated, cross-agency answer to disaster recovery once the emergency response ends — case management that connects a household to every partner it needs, instead of one at a time.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing an FWRD disaster case manager — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Home-Delivered Meals (Meals on Wheels of Brevard/Transylvania)
orgs.public_description: Prepared meals delivered to the homes of neighbors who cannot easily shop or cook — most often homebound older adults — on a sliding-scale basis. The same driver each week means the meal comes with a wellness check.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Meals on Wheels coordinator or driver — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Behavioral Health Access & Crisis Line (Vaya Health)
orgs.public_description: The number you call in a behavioral-health crisis, and the entity that connects a family to counseling and covers it. Not a therapist's office — it runs the 24/7 crisis line and mobile crisis, does same-day walk-in assessment, manages care, and routes people to the adult and youth behavioral-health doors.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Vaya care manager / crisis-line navigator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Legal Aid / Benefits Appeals (Pisgah Legal Services)
orgs.public_description: Free civil legal help for the paperwork walls that block care and stability — benefits denials and appeals, Medicaid and disability determinations, housing and eviction, and disaster-recovery claims.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Pisgah Legal advocate — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

orgs.display_name: Community Health Worker (Transylvania County DSS / CHW program)
orgs.public_description: A trained, trusted navigator who meets families where they are — a home visit, a phone call, a walk into an office — and actually closes the loop: helps enroll in benefits, books the ride, tracks the referral the family cannot see, and follows up. The formal, funded version of the connector role.
orgs.represented_by_note: Volunteer playing a Community Health Worker or DSS navigator — real-org partner, confirm participation before event day

resources.name: Cardiology Practice (Henderson County)
resources.public_description: A cardiology practice one county away. Referral required; records must arrive first.
resources.eligibility: Accepts Medicare; referral and records must arrive before booking is confirmed.
resources.hours: Weekdays 8–5

_internal.partner_notes: Portal pre-registration strongly encouraged by the practice.
_internal.internal_note: Composite practice — do not name a real clinic in participant materials.

resources.name: Transylvania County Transportation
resources.public_description: The county transportation service runs a fixed weekday route for $1 — but any trip off that route, or out of county, must be booked days ahead and costs more, if it is available at all.
resources.eligibility: Fixed route through Brevard/Rosman weekdays ~6:30am–4:30pm, $1 exact-cash per boarding (22 Brevard + 5 Rosman stops). Anything OFF the fixed route — a medical trip, an out-of-county specialist, a rural-home pickup — is demand-response/paratransit that must be reserved in advance (typically 24–48 hours) for a higher fee, and same-day or out-of-county trips may not be available at all. Dedicated medical transportation prioritizes ages 60+ and those with no other means.
resources.hours: Fixed route weekdays ~6:30am–4:30pm; medical transportation by request, (828) 884-3203 option 2

_internal.partner_notes: Branded "Transylvania in Motion (TIM)." Ride availability effectively sets the care timeline for carless households — capacity tightened further after Brevard City Cab ceased operations, pushing more demand onto the county system.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from transylvaniacounty.org/departments/transportation. Confirm current schedule and eligibility with the department before event day.

resources.name: County Behavioral Health Provider
resources.public_description: The county behavioral health office — skilled, caring, and carrying a long waitlist.
resources.eligibility: Sliding scale available; youth evaluations require guardian intake.
resources.hours: Weekdays; waitlist ~10 weeks for new evaluations

_internal.partner_notes: Cancellation list and school-based telehealth exist but are under-known.
_internal.internal_note: Waitlist number is an estimate; verify before public use.

resources.name: School Counseling & Skills Groups
resources.public_description: Counseling check-ins and skills groups at school, usually available within days.
resources.eligibility: Enrolled students; parent consent for groups.
resources.hours: School days

_internal.partner_notes: Fastest available bridge support for school-age kids; not a substitute for clinical evaluation.

resources.name: The Sharing House
resources.public_description: The Sharing House: a central location for food, clothing, and supplies, with a short first-time intake.
resources.eligibility: Short intake; household-size based. Dietary flags (low-sodium etc.) accommodated. Also provides clothing and other supplies (Transylvania Christian Ministry).
resources.hours: Confirm current pickup schedule with the organization before event day

_internal.partner_notes: Warm referrals cut intake from ~20 minutes to ~2.
_internal.internal_note: Web-verified 2026-07-08 (sharinghouse.org, findhelp.org, Transylvania Times). Public listings show 164 Duckworth Ave, Brevard; hours Mon–Fri 9am–4pm (closed 12–1); (828) 884-2866; food/clothing/financial assistance and appointment-based food orders — all consistent with the app. Confirm current pickup schedule and intake details with The Sharing House directly before public use.

resources.name: Bread of Life
resources.public_description: Bread of Life: same-day food help, hot meals, no questions asked.
resources.eligibility: Name and household size only. No documentation, no questions asked. Runs a food truck reaching remote areas of the county.
resources.hours: Weekdays — hot meals and pantry staples; confirm current hours with the organization

_internal.partner_notes: Designed as a bridge to the weekly pantry, not a replacement. Since 1996; also serves hot meals daily.
_internal.internal_note: Web-verified 2026-07-08 (breadoflifetc.org, foodpantries.org, Transylvania Times). Public listings show a FIXED location (238 South Caldwell St, Brevard) with hot meals Mon–Fri 12–2pm and donation intake 8:30–11:30am. The "no questions asked" framing is corroborated, but the "food truck reaching remote areas" claim in eligibility_notes is NOT supported by any public source found — treat as unverified and remove from any participant copy until Bread of Life confirms it directly. Confirm hours/capacity directly before public use.

resources.name: Hunger Coalition of Transylvania County
resources.public_description: The Hunger Coalition brings food to a different part of the county each Thursday.
resources.eligibility: Rotating pantry, a different location each Thursday; partners with MANNA Food Bank and the Transylvania Farmers' Market for fresh produce.
resources.hours: First, second, third, and fourth Thursdays — location rotates

_internal.partner_notes: The rotation model exists specifically to reach households for whom getting to a fixed pantry is the barrier.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from hungerfreetc.com. Confirm current rotation schedule with the organization before event day.

resources.name: Resilience Hub Navigation
resources.public_description: Tell your story once. The Hub maps the path and calls ahead so every next door expects you.
resources.eligibility: Open door. No eligibility screening to talk.
resources.hours: Weekdays 9–5, some evenings

_internal.partner_notes: The Hub listens once and carries the story forward — navigation and warm handoffs, not clinical care.
_internal.internal_note: The Hub is the visible anchor; the ecosystem is the story. Never describe it as replacing providers.

resources.name: Transylvania Public Health
resources.public_description: The county health department — immunizations, WIC, and programs many residents don't know they qualify for.
resources.eligibility: Immunizations, WIC, environmental health, and home-visit programs; open to county residents.
resources.hours: Mon–Thu 8:30am–12pm & 1–5pm

_internal.partner_notes: 106 E Morgan St, Brevard — administrative and environmental health on floor 1, personal health services and WIC on floor 3.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from transylvaniahealth.org. Confirm current programs/hours with the department before public use.

resources.name: Blue Ridge Health — Family Medicine
resources.public_description: A sliding-scale clinic that sees families regardless of ability to pay.
resources.eligibility: FQHC — sliding-scale fees for uninsured/underinsured patients. Also offers nutrition services and medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD).
resources.hours: Tue/Thu/Fri 8–5, Mon/Wed 8–8 (per public listing)

_internal.partner_notes: 29 West French Broad St, Suite 203, Brevard. (828) 883-5550.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from brchs.com. Confirm participation, hours, and sliding-scale details directly with Blue Ridge Health before public use.

resources.name: Blue Ridge Health — Pediatrics
resources.public_description: Blue Ridge Health's pediatric clinic — sliding scale, portal-based scheduling.
resources.eligibility: FQHC pediatric care, sliding scale. Same organization runs the county's school-based health centers.
resources.hours: Tue/Thu/Fri 8–5, Mon/Wed 8–8 (per public listing)

_internal.partner_notes: 29 West French Broad St, Suite 203, Brevard. Portal-based scheduling; no confirmed interpreter line as of this writing.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from brchs.com. Bilingual/interpreter capacity NOT confirmed — do not claim it publicly until Blue Ridge Health confirms directly.

resources.name: Storm Recovery Assistance Application
resources.public_description: A recovery assistance application — real, but paperwork-heavy, with documentation requirements that are easy to miss.
resources.eligibility: Documentation-heavy intake; homeowner or renter applicants for storm/flood-related damage.
resources.hours: Rolling application window

_internal.partner_notes: A second set of eyes on the paperwork measurably reduces "returned for missing documentation" cycles.
_internal.internal_note: Composite process modeled generally on the concept of a disaster-recovery application/intake step. Tropical Storm Helene (Sept. 2024) is now named directly elsewhere in this packet (see env-storm-aftermath and the long_term_recovery station/FWRD Transylvania) — this specific application step remains a composite stand-in, not a named real fund or program.

resources.name: Transylvania Habitat for Humanity — Recovery Repairs
resources.public_description: Habitat for Humanity's recovery-repair program — real help, on a volunteer-and-materials timeline, not an instant one.
resources.eligibility: Homeowners with storm/flood-related repair needs; volunteer-labor and donated-materials dependent, so scheduling runs on a queue rather than a fixed calendar.
resources.hours: Confirm current intake process with the organization before event day

_internal.partner_notes: A warm handoff with the paperwork already in order moves a household onto the repair queue faster than a cold application.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from the Transylvania Nonprofit Sector Analysis (2026), which documents Habitat for Humanity supporting home repairs for storm-impacted homeowners in the county. Tropical Storm Helene (Sept. 2024) is now named directly in participant copy (decision, 2026-07-07 — see env-storm-aftermath and REAL_ORG_OUTREACH_MAP.md). Confirm current program details directly with Habitat before public use.

resources.name: El Centro Comunitario Hispano-Americano
resources.public_description: El Centro — the county's Hispanic-serving organization. Someone here always answers in Spanish.
resources.eligibility: Open door; serves the Hispanic community and connects families to broader county resources. Runs a Homework Club and Club Acción for youth.
resources.hours: Confirm current hours with the organization before event day

_internal.partner_notes: A Spanish speaker always answers the phone — the county's only Hispanic-serving organization historically.
_internal.internal_note: Web-verified 2026-07-08 (elcentrobrevard.com, Idealist, NC Center for Nonprofits). Address 249 E Main St corroborated; phone (828) 585-7018; Latino-led; services include resource referral, homework/ESL/tutoring, translation, and disaster relief — consistent with the app (the specific "Club Acción" program name was not independently confirmed). Public hours not listed. Needs direct confirmation from El Centro before naming/staffing them at the convening.

resources.name: Transylvania County DSS — Benefits & Enrollment
resources.public_description: The county benefits office — Medicaid, food assistance, and emergency energy help, with a real processing timeline attached.
resources.eligibility: Administers Medicaid, SNAP (Food and Nutrition Services), WorkFirst, Child Care Subsidy, and Energy Assistance for county residents.
resources.hours: Confirm current hours with the department before event day

_internal.partner_notes: 106 E Morgan St, Brevard — same building as Transylvania Public Health. (828) 884-3174. Medicaid applications can take up to 45 days to process.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from transylvaniacounty.org/departments/social-services and ncdhhs.gov local DSS directory. Confirm current processing times and program list directly with DSS before public use.

resources.name: The Haven of Transylvania County
resources.public_description: A real shelter with a real intake process — a bed for tonight, and help pointed toward something permanent.
resources.eligibility: 18-bed overnight shelter for homeless men, women, and children. Intake interviews by appointment Mon–Thu; all applicants complete an intake interview and background check.
resources.hours: Intake interviews Monday–Thursday, by appointment

_internal.partner_notes: 126 Oakdale St, Brevard. (828) 877-2040. Offers evening meal, light breakfast, laundry, showers, mail/phone messaging, and referral toward permanent or transitional housing.
_internal.internal_note: Web-verified 2026-07-08 (havenoftc.org, homelessshelterdirectory.org, GuideStar). Address 126 Oakdale St, phone (828) 877-2040, and the intake-interview-plus-background-check process (by appointment Mon–Thu) all corroborated. NUANCE: public listings describe the 18-bed "Thomas House" as serving single adults; the "men, women, and children" phrasing in eligibility_notes likely anticipates the forthcoming "House of Hope" family expansion (advertised as coming soon, not yet open). Soften to single adults, or confirm the family-capacity timeline with the Haven, before public use.

resources.name: Meridian Behavioral Health Services — Adult Outpatient
resources.public_description: Outpatient counseling and care coordination for adults — real, local support, though not a detox or residential program.
resources.eligibility: Outpatient counseling (individual, group, family) and care coordination for adults, including substance-use concerns. Not a detox or residential treatment program.
resources.hours: Confirm current hours with the organization before event day

_internal.partner_notes: Part of Blue Ridge Health — Meridian became a Blue Ridge Health subsidiary in the 2021 merger; this is BRH's behavioral-health arm, not an independent org. 69 North Broad Street, Brevard. (828) 883-2708. Tailored Care Management connects Medicaid Tailored Plan/Direct recipients with substance-use or behavioral-health concerns to community resources.
_internal.internal_note: Web-verified 2026-07-08 (brchs.com, HRSA connector, Transylvania Times). CORRECTION: Meridian Behavioral Health Services merged into Blue Ridge Health in Oct 2021 and is now BRH's behavioral-health arm — NOT an independent org, and the old mbhci.org identity is stale. Address 69 N Broad St and phone (828) 883-2708 corroborated. If named at the convening, coordinate through Blue Ridge Health and frame as "Meridian Behavioral Health Services, part of Blue Ridge Health." County still has no detox/residential program — confirm adult scope before public use.

resources.name: Through the Trees — Digital Access
resources.public_description: A refurbished device, help with the internet bill, and someone to sit with you through the parts that don't make sense.
resources.eligibility: Refurbished device matching, digital literacy training, and help enrolling in internet-cost assistance programs; also subsidizes broadband expansion/monthly costs for low-income households.
resources.hours: Retail storefront on Main Street, Brevard — confirm current hours before event day

_internal.partner_notes: 2025 Brevard/Transylvania Chamber of Commerce Nonprofit of the Year. Over 1,600 devices distributed across Buncombe, Henderson, and Transylvania counties as of last count.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from throughthetrees.us, ncruralcenter.org, and ednc.org coverage. Confirm current program details and capacity directly with Through the Trees before public use.

resources.name: Brevard/Transylvania Chamber of Commerce — Workforce Development
resources.public_description: Training pathways and a connection to local employers — a bridge toward a job that pays enough.
resources.eligibility: NCWorks Next Gen (youth-focused) and the Customized Training program, delivered with Blue Ridge Community College, connecting residents to training pathways and employers.
resources.hours: 175 E Main St, Brevard — confirm current hours before event day

_internal.partner_notes: Serving the business community since 1923; over 475 members. (828) 883-3700.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from brevardncchamber.org and justeconomicswnc.org. Confirm current program list and eligibility directly with the Chamber before public use.

resources.name: FWRD Transylvania — Long-Term Recovery Group
resources.public_description: A team that coordinates your recovery case across every partner involved, instead of you explaining it fresh at each one.
resources.eligibility: Coordinates disaster case management, unmet-needs identification, and cross-agency recovery support for households affected by Tropical Storm Helene (Sept. 2024); also runs community preparedness workshops.
resources.hours: Confirm current hours/intake process with the organization before event day

_internal.partner_notes: Formerly the Transylvania County Long-Term Recovery Group; formed with support from the American Red Cross, FEMA, NCVOAD, Dogwood Health Trust, and others. Represents the "long-term recovery group" category broadly — FWRD is Transylvania County's specific instance of it.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from gofwrd.org. FWRD's public identity is explicitly tied to Helene recovery, which is why storm references elsewhere in this packet (env-storm-aftermath, Linda's route) now name Tropical Storm Helene directly rather than staying generic (decision made 2026-07-07 — see REAL_ORG_OUTREACH_MAP.md). Confirm current scope and capacity directly with FWRD before public use.

resources.name: Meals on Wheels of Brevard/Transylvania — Home-Delivered Meals
resources.public_description: A hot meal brought to your door by the same person each week — who would notice if you did not answer.
resources.eligibility: For homebound residents (often older adults or people with disabilities) who cannot easily shop or prepare meals. Sliding-scale/donation-based; a brief eligibility screening applies.
resources.hours: Weekday delivery routes; meals prepared at Transylvania Regional Hospital. Confirm current capacity and any waitlist before event day.

_internal.partner_notes: Delivered by a large volunteer driver corps on consistent weekly routes, so delivery doubles as a wellness check for isolated neighbors.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from mealsonwheelsbrevard.org. Confirm eligibility, cost model, and capacity directly with the organization before public use.

resources.name: Vaya Health — Behavioral Health Access, Care Management & Crisis
resources.public_description: The number you call in a crisis, and the people who help you find a counselor and cover the cost.
resources.eligibility: Public managed care organization (MCO) for behavioral health, mental health, substance use, I/DD, and TBI. Runs a 24/7 crisis line, mobile crisis, and same-day walk-in crisis assessment; manages Medicaid behavioral-health benefits and connects members to providers. Serves anyone in crisis regardless of coverage.
resources.hours: 24/7 behavioral-health crisis line; member/recipient line weekdays and Saturdays. Confirm local walk-in / mobile crisis details before event day.

_internal.partner_notes: Selected as the NC ROOTS rural-health-transformation hub lead for Region 3. Vaya and Partners Health Management are merging effective Oct. 1, 2026 — naming may change.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from vayahealth.com. Vaya is an MCO / care-management / crisis entity, NOT a direct therapy provider — keep that distinction. Confirm current crisis-access details and post-merger identity before public use.

resources.name: Pisgah Legal Services — Free Civil Legal Aid & Benefits Appeals
resources.public_description: Free help to appeal a denial and make the system look at your case again.
resources.eligibility: Free civil legal assistance for low-income WNC residents: benefits denials and appeals (Medicaid, disability, SNAP), housing and eviction, domestic-safety, and disaster-recovery legal issues. Income-based eligibility.
resources.hours: Serves Transylvania County from regional offices and clinics; confirm current intake process and any local hours before event day.

_internal.partner_notes: Regional legal-aid nonprofit covering multiple WNC counties; a wrongly denied benefit can often be reversed on appeal with advocacy.
_internal.internal_note: Sourced from pisgahlegal.org (verify current Transylvania County intake and scope directly before public use).

resources.name: Community Health Worker Navigation (Transylvania County DSS)
resources.public_description: Someone whose actual job is to hold the thread of your case — the calls, the forms, the follow-up.
resources.eligibility: Trained community health workers provide active navigation — benefits enrollment help, appointment and transportation coordination, referral follow-up, and home visits. Often housed at or partnered with the county Department of Social Services.
resources.hours: Weekday outreach and by referral; confirm current CHW program capacity and intake before event day.

_internal.partner_notes: Community Health Worker is an increasingly funded, Medicaid-recognized role in NC. The value here is loop-closing: the CHW carries the task instead of assigning it.
_internal.internal_note: Added 2026-07-15 (Jeff) to provide a real navigation SERVICE door distinct from the Referral Desk friction point. Confirm the county's current CHW program and any DSS partnership before public use.
